t-pot.explanation: The total amount of chips all players have contributed to the current pot

t-blinds.explanation: Mandatory preflop bets (SB and BB) that create the initial pot

t-stack.explanation: The total number of chips a player currently holds

t-position.explanation: A player's seat at the table, which determines the order of action

t-buyin.explanation: The amount of chips required to enter a cash game or tournament

t-showdown.explanation: The phase after the river where remaining players reveal their hands to compare

t-community.explanation: The five shared cards in the center of the table used by all players

t-holecards.explanation: The two private face-down cards dealt to each player

t-dealer.explanation: The round disc that marks the current dealer position

t-rake.explanation: The service fee the casino/platform takes from the pot

t-suited.explanation: Two hole cards of the same suit (e.g. Ah Kh), written as "s"

t-offsuit.explanation: Two hole cards of different suits (e.g. Ah Kd), written as "o"

t-connector.explanation: Two cards with adjacent ranks (e.g. JTs, 89o) with straight potential

t-pocketpair.explanation: Two hole cards of the same rank (e.g. AA, 77, 22)

t-gapper.explanation: Cards one or two ranks apart (e.g. J9 = one gapper, T7 = two gapper)

t-broadway.explanation: Any two cards from T-J-Q-K-A (e.g. AK, QJ, AT)

t-rag.explanation: A worthless small hand (e.g. 72o, 83o) to fold from any position

t-nuts.explanation: The absolute strongest hand possible on the current board

t-draw.explanation: A hand one card away from a strong hand (e.g. flush draw, straight draw)

t-outs.explanation: The number of remaining cards that can improve your hand (e.g. 9 outs for a flush draw)

t-open.explanation: The first raise preflop (as opposed to just calling the blind)

t-3bet.explanation: A re-raise against an open raise (the third betting action preflop)

t-cbet.explanation: A continuation bet made postflop by the preflop raiser

t-checkraise.explanation: Checking to let an opponent bet, then raising (a powerful move)

t-slowplay.explanation: Deliberately checking/calling with a strong hand to conceal its strength

t-float.explanation: Calling a flop C-Bet with a weak hand, planning to steal the pot on the turn

t-donkbet.explanation: Betting out of position into the aggressor postflop (often seen as a weak play)

t-squeeze.explanation: A large re-raise against one raise and one or more calls

t-limp.explanation: Merely calling the big blind preflop instead of raising (often considered a weak play)

t-ev.explanation: The average profit/loss of a decision repeated over the long run

t-range.explanation: The set of all hands a player might hold

t-equity.explanation: The probability that your hand wins against an opponent's range

t-potodds.explanation: The ratio of the call amount to the total pot (determines whether a call is profitable)

t-impliedodds.explanation: Effective odds that account for additional profit on future streets

t-gto.explanation: Game Theory Optimal — an unexploitable strategy that cannot be beaten no matter how the opponent plays

t-exploitative.explanation: A strategy adjusted to exploit specific opponent weaknesses

t-variance.explanation: The fluctuation of short-term results around long-term expectation

t-tilt.explanation: Making irrational decisions due to emotional swings caused by negative events

t-bankroll.explanation: Money reserved specifically for playing poker, kept separate from living expenses

t-vpip.explanation: The frequency of voluntarily putting money into the pot (excluding forced blinds)

t-pfr.explanation: The frequency of raising preflop voluntarily

t-icm.explanation: Independent Chip Model — converts chips into real monetary value in tournaments

t-mdf.explanation: Minimum Defense Frequency — the lowest fraction of your range you must continue with (call or raise, never fold) facing a bet, so the opponent cannot auto-profit bluffing with any two cards. Formula: MDF = 1 - bet/(pot + bet), equivalently pot/(pot + bet); with b = bet as a fraction of pot, MDF = 1/(1+b). Example: facing a 1/2-pot bet, MDF = 1/1.5 = 67%. The larger the bet, the lower the frequency you must continue at. MDF is a safety net against over-folding, not a rule to follow blindly.

t-alpha.explanation: Alpha — the fold frequency a pure bluff needs from the opponent in order to break even (EV = 0); this is the attacker's side of the same coin as MDF. Formula: Alpha = bet/(pot + bet), i.e. b/(1+b). Example: a 1/2-pot bluff needs Alpha = 33% folds to be automatically profitable. Alpha and MDF are complements (MDF + Alpha = 1) and point in opposite directions: MDF belongs to the defender, Alpha to the aggressor. Do not confuse either with the equity needed to call, bet/(pot + 2*bet), which has a different denominator.

t-spr.explanation: Stack-to-Pot Ratio — formula: SPR = effective stack / pot size. Bands: SPR below 4 is low (top pair is worth committing), 4-10 is medium (standard play), above 10 is high (deep stacks, speculative hands such as suited connectors gain value). Example: 200BB effective against a 15BB pot on the flop gives SPR = 13.3. 3-Bet pots usually play at SPR 3-6 while single-raised pots sit around 8-15.

t-polarized.explanation: One of the two basic range shapes: it contains only strong hands (the nuts or near-nuts) plus bluff hands that are air and carry blockers, and no medium-strength hands (polarized = strong + weak, nothing in between). Typical spots: large river bets and overbets, preflop 3-bet/4-bet, check-raise. Rule: the bigger the sizing, the more polarized the range; the smaller the sizing, the more merged it is. A polarized range pairs with large sizings (above 2/3 pot).

t-mergedrange.explanation: Merged / Linear range — the shape opposite to polarized: a continuous distribution from strong down to medium strength (strong + medium, no air), bet at mixed frequency. Rule: small sizings (below 1/2 pot) suit merged ranges, since the goal is to charge the opponent's entire continuation range at the lowest possible cost and take thin value, while keeping a cheap showdown path for your own medium-strength hands.

t-overbet.explanation: A bet sized larger than the current pot (typically 125%-200% pot). Its core precondition is a nuts advantage: your range contains super-strong hands that cannot exist in the opponent's range. The range must be polarized (top value plus bluff hands with blockers), with a value-to-bluff ratio around 2:1 — facing a 150% pot overbet the opponent's MDF is only 40%, so you cannot bluff too much.

t-blocker.explanation: Cards in your hand that remove combinations of specific hands from the opponent's range. Example: there are only four aces, so holding one ace cuts the opponent's AA combos from 6 to 3 and AK from 16 to 12. This is why A5s makes a better 3-bet bluff than 76s. In bluff catching: blocking the opponent's value range means they are more likely to be bluffing, so you lean to calling; blocking their bluff range means they are more likely to have value, so you lean to folding.

t-equityrealization.explanation: Equity Realization — the share of your raw equity you actually get to cash in. This is the essence of position advantage: the same 50% raw equity realizes above 100% in position and typically only 80-90% out of position. A second dimension: the deeper the stacks, the less high pairs (AA/KK) realize postflop, while suited connectors gain playability.

t-semibluff.explanation: Betting or raising with a draw — you are not ahead right now, but you have outs to overtake on a later street. Two ways to win: the opponent folds and you take the pot immediately (fold equity), or they call and you improve to the best hand and win a large pot (equity realization). Best to worst bluff hands: combination draws (flush + straight) > flush draws > open-ended straight draws > gutshots.

t-foldequity.explanation: Fold Equity — the share of expectation you earn when the opponent folds and you take the pot outright. Calculation: fold equity = probability the opponent folds x pot size. It is one of the two profit sources when betting with draws and air hands (the other is equity realization), and it is exactly what the pure-bluff break-even threshold Alpha = bet/(pot + bet) measures.

t-rangeadvantage.explanation: Range Advantage — on a given board texture one player's whole range has a higher average equity than the other's. It drives sizing and frequency: a dry high-card board (such as K-7-2 rainbow) usually gives the preflop aggressor a range advantage, allowing a small sizing across the whole range at high frequency. It often moves together with a nuts advantage but not always, so judge them separately.

t-nutsadvantage.explanation: Nuts Advantage — one player's range contains the strongest possible combinations (sets, big two pairs, nut flushes) that cannot exist in the opponent's range. Example: you check-raise a K-7-2 flop and the turn is another K, so your range holds KK/77 while the opponent's cannot. This is the core precondition for overbetting. Unlike a range advantage, which compares average equity, a nuts advantage compares density at the very top of the range.
